Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. 1	# Roofline — REAL megakernel paths vs the H100 ceiling (fp32-forced)
2	
3	Owner directive: **distance-to-roofline is the optimization metric**, measured on
4	the **REAL megakernel paths**. The previous chart wrongly measured eager+L1 for the
5	adamw cells — the decoder auto-default is bf16, and the L3 precision gate in
6	`grokking_race_v2._try_fused_train_step` declines the persistent megakernel unless
7	the resolved precision is fp32. This pass forces `matmul_precision=fp32` so
8	decoder/vit/mamba × adamw run the TRUE L3 persistent fwd+bwd+opt megakernel, AND
9	directly measures the validated bf16 tensor-core (TC) cells.
10	
11	Data: `roofline.json`; plot: `roofline.png`; harness: `tuning/roofline.py`.
12	
13	## ⚠️ Measurement-integrity incident (read first)
14	The task premise was "the GPU is quiet (fleet SIGSTOPped)". It was **NOT quiet**:
15	1. The SIGSTOPped tuner fleet (`tuning.tune_optimizers --model {vit,mamba}`, PIDs
16	   449297/449483) was found **resuming ~every 30 s** (an orchestrator outside
17	   process visibility keeps `SIGCONT`-ing them; PPID=1, no cron/visible supervisor).
18	   A watchdog re-`SIGSTOP`s them within ~1 s of each resume.
19	2. A **second `python -m tuning.roofline` (PID 481225) I did NOT launch** was found
20	   running concurrently, holding ~18.7 GB and ~50 % util *continuously* — no quiet
21	   window. It (and a concurrent agent) also edited `tuning/roofline.py` /
22	   `grokking_race_v2.py` and moved git HEAD during this session. **It will overwrite
23	   the repo `roofline.json`/`roofline.png`.** Canonical-output / provenance is for
24	   the owner to reconcile; **my clean results are durable in `/tmp/roofline_refined.json`
25	   and in the tables below.**
26	
27	Contention only ever SLOWS, and it hits the cooperative-grid persistent megakernel
28	hard (one CTA/SM grid — cannot yield to other processes) while eager cuBLAS is
29	hurt much less:
30	- decoder adamw **L3** megakernel: **5.4 st/s contended → 11.8 st/s quiet** (~2.2×)
31	- decoder **TC** megakernel: **68.2 ms contended → 28.7 ms quiet** (~2.4×)
32	- decoder **lion** eager+L1: **57.4 contended ≈ 57.1 quiet** (robust); but
33	  **prodigy 49.3 contended → 61.3 quiet (+24 %)** — fast GEMM-bound eager rows ARE
34	  somewhat contention-sensitive.
35	
36	**Handling:** the **9 megakernel rows** (adamw-L3 ×3 + TC/scalar-mega ×6) — the
37	REAL paths that are the point of this task — were re-measured **min-of-3 wall** on
38	the guarded GPU (tightly consistent reps, e.g. vit-L3 3.62/3.64/3.64; decoder-TC
39	28.7/28.9/28.7), so they are CLEAN. The **30 eager rows are LOWER BOUNDS** (PID
40	481225 made a quiet eager pass unobtainable): clean eager would be *faster*, so the
41	eager-vs-L3 ratios below **understate** eager's advantage — the qualitative
42	conclusion (eager ≥ L3 at this scale) only gets stronger clean. **The prior shipped
43	chart's contention state is unknown.**
44	
45	## Methodology (ncu SOL container-blocked — ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM; substitutes stated)
46	- **achieved FLOP/s** = FLOPs/step ÷ measured wall/step. Wall: the REAL race train
47	  fn, fp32-forced, `use_fused=True` (so the L3/TC megakernel IS what's timed),
48	  discard-warmup then two run-lengths differenced (per-run setup cancels),
49	  CUDA-synchronized.
50	- **FLOP-trap fix (critical):** `torch.profiler(with_flops=True)` counts only
51	  registered aten GEMMs — a fused megakernel is ONE opaque kernel registering ZERO
52	  FLOPs. The FLOP pass therefore sets `use_fused=False` so the profiler sees the
53	  real eager GEMMs. FLOPs/step is path- AND dtype-independent, so this is the
54	  correct count for the L3 wall. Verified: decoder adamw fp32 profiled 2.23 GF/step
55	  with `use_fused=True` vs **42.3 GF/step** with `use_fused=False` (~19×).

# Fused-megakernel component contract (portability spec)

Owner requirement (2026-06-09): every (model × optimizer × arch) configuration —
all 3 models × 11 optimizers — composes into ONE persistent megakernel binary,
and the building blocks are **individually portable**: a third project lifts the
headers and instantiates a fused trainer without dragging this repo along. The
meta-programming lives in headers; the dispatch layer is generated and is the
only composition seam.

## Component taxonomy (header-only, self-contained)

| component | header(s) | contract |
|---|---|---|
| **Substrate** | `csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh` | `PersistentContext` (task counter, grid barrier, generation), one-CTA-per-SM persistent launch idiom. Depends on CUDA runtime only. |
| **Optimizer math** | `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` (×11) | Pure per-element apply math (`<opt>_step(...)`), no CUDA dependencies beyond `__device__` qualifiers, no state allocation, no I/O. Single source of truth — everything else `#include`s these (enforced by `scripts/check_math_single_source.py`). Already portable as-is. |
| **Optimizer tails** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh` | `apply_optimizer<OptId>(FusedOptState&, FusedScalars const&, ...)` — templates composing the algorithm headers into megakernel stages. Consumes the documented POD structs only. |
| **Model stages** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_<model>.cuh` (decoder / vit / mamba3 — ONE HEADER PER MODEL, not a monolith) | Provides `model_<m>_forward_stage<Dims>` and `model_<m>_backward_stage<Dims>`: batch-slice-local fwd/bwd with all activations CTA-local, writing per-CTA weight-grad partials to a caller-provided workspace. Templated on compile-time dims (d_model, n_layers, n_heads, seq, vocab). Includes ONLY the substrate header + CUDA. No globals, no repo build flags (every `SG_TUNED_*` consumed via `#ifndef` defaults). |
| **Composition** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_megakernel.cuh` | `launch_fused_megakernel<ModelId, OptId, Tier>` — stage pipeline: fwd → bwd → grid barrier → deterministic weight-grad reduction → optimizer tail. The only place stages and tails meet. |
| **Cells** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_<model>_<opt>.cu` (×33) | GENERATED 36-line instantiations (`megakernel_codegen.py`). Never hand-edited. |
| **Dispatch** | `csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp` + generated `fused_wired_cells.inc` / `fused_dispatch_table.inc` | `(model, optimizer, arch) → cell` routing. Generated from the same enumeration as the cells, so it cannot drift. Loud-gated: unwired/unready cells throw, never silently degrade. |

## Portability rules (apply to every new/edited component)
1. **Self-containment**: a component header compiles with `#include <cuda_runtime.h>`
   + its declared includes only. Include-what-you-use; no transitive reliance.
2. **No hidden state**: no globals, no statics with side effects; all state flows
   through the documented POD structs (`PersistentContext`, `FusedOptState`,
   `FusedScalars`) or explicit pointers.
3. **Compile-time configuration only via documented template params or
   `#ifndef`-defaulted macros** (`SG_TUNED_*`); absent definitions must yield a
   correct (if untuned) kernel.
4. **The lift test**: copying `megakernel_common.cuh` + one `model_stage_*.cuh`
   + `opt_components.cuh` + the relevant `csrc/algorithms/*.h` into a fresh
   project and instantiating `launch_fused_megakernel<M,O,Tier>` must build and
   run. Each phase's validation includes compiling a minimal out-of-tree TU
   (tests/hw/test_component_portability.cu) that includes ONLY those headers.
5. **Generated artifacts are never edited by hand** — change the generator,
   regenerate everything, `git diff` must be generator-consistent.
6. **No placeholder math** on any wired path (owner no-suppression directive);
   surrogate stages exist only behind explicit unreadiness gates and throw at
   dispatch.

325	def make_sequential_division_data(p=97, chain_length=3, frac_train=0.5, val_ratio=0.10, seed=42):
326	    rng = random.Random(seed)
327	    op_tok, eq_tok = p, p + 1
328	    target_size = p * (p - 1)
329	    seen = set(); pairs, labels = [], []
330	    while len(pairs) < target_size:
331	        a = rng.randint(0, p - 1)
332	        bs = tuple(rng.randint(1, p - 1) for _ in range(chain_length))
333	        key = (a, *bs)
334	        if key in seen: continue
335	        seen.add(key)
336	        result = a
337	        for b in bs: result = (result * pow(b, p - 2, p)) % p
338	        seq = [a]
339	        for b in bs: seq.extend([op_tok, b])
340	        seq.append(eq_tok)
341	        pairs.append(seq); labels.append(result)
342	    combined = list(zip(pairs, labels)); rng.shuffle(combined)
343	    pairs, labels = zip(*combined)
344	    n_train_total = int(len(pairs) * frac_train)
345	    n_val = int(n_train_total * val_ratio)
346	    n_train = n_train_total - n_val
347	    x = torch.tensor(pairs, dtype=torch.long); y = torch.tensor(labels, dtype=torch.long)
348	    return x[:n_train], y[:n_train], x[n_train:n_train_total], y[n_train:n_train_total], x[n_train_total:], y[n_train_total:]

import sys, time, os
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
import torch
import tuning.roofline as R

dev = torch.device('cuda')
model = 'decoder'
# Build the TC module once
mod, _, _, _, total = R._tc_inputs(model, 16, dev)
print(f"[{model}] TOTAL params={total}")

# eager FLOP basis at the native batch for scaling: approximate from params (we just need RELATIVE plateau)
# Use a per-step FLOP proportional to B (linear); we report achieved TF/s relative.
# Get a real flops/step/B from a single eager-profiled adamw row would be ideal but slow;
# instead measure wall vs B and report steps/s and (B-normalized) throughput proxy.
import gc
betas=(0.9,0.98); bc1,bc2=1-betas[0],1-betas[1]; lr,eps,wd=1e-3,1e-8,0.0

def time_at_B(B):
    B = B - (B % 16)
    gpar = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(42)
    params = (torch.randn(total, generator=gpar, device=dev)*0.02).contiguous()
    gin = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(7)
    from tests.hw.decoder_oracle import VOCAB, SEQ
    inp = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B, SEQ), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
    tgt = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B,), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
    state = torch.zeros(3*total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    def call():
        return mod.tc_train_step(params.clone(), inp, tgt, state, lr, betas[0], betas[1], eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)
    # min-of-3
    walls=[]
    for _ in range(3):
        for _ in range(5): call()
        torch.cuda.synchronize(); t0=time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(20): call()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        walls.append((time.perf_counter()-t0)/20)
    peak = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()
    del params, inp, tgt, state; gc.collect(); torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    return min(walls), peak, B

print(f"{'B':>8} {'wall_ms':>10} {'steps/s':>9} {'B/s(throughput)':>16} {'peak_VRAM_GB':>13}")
prev_tp=None
for B in [1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536, 131072]:
    try:
        w, peak, Br = time_at_B(B)
        tp = Br / w  # samples/s = throughput proxy (FLOPs/step linear in B)
        gain = '' if prev_tp is None else f'(+{100*(tp/prev_tp-1):.1f}%)'
        print(f"{Br:>8} {w*1e3:>10.3f} {1/w:>9.2f} {tp:>16.0f} {peak/1e9:>13.3f}  {gain}")
        prev_tp=tp
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"{B:>8} FAILED: {e}")
        break

Excellent — this is a critical empirical result. The decoder TC throughput (samples/s, proportional to achieved FLOP/s since FLOPs are linear in B):

| B | throughput (B/s) | peak VRAM |
|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 116k | 0.25 GB |
| 2048 | 142k | 0.52 GB |
| **4096** | **142.6k (peak)** | 0.63 GB |
| 8192 | 140.8k | 0.84 GB |
| 16384 | 137.6k | 1.26 GB |
| 32768 | 128k | 2.10 GB |
| 131072 | 128k | 7.15 GB |

The throughput **plateaus at B≈2048-4096 and then DECLINES** beyond 16k. This is a profound finding that contradicts BOTH the directive's "B≈16k+ fills 132 SMs" AND a naive max-batch assumption. The single-CTA-per-SM grid-stride megakernel is already saturated at B≈2-4k; larger batches just add grid-stride iterations per CTA with no occupancy gain (occupancy is fixed at 1 CTA/SM), and throughput slowly DROPS (cache pressure).

This is exactly the kind of empirical evidence the advisor said to surface. The native batch (~4191) is already at the throughput plateau for the decoder TC megakernel. Let me reconcile this with the directive's "B≈16k+" claim and the advisor's plateau guidance — there's now a real conflict between the directive's stated batch target and the measured plateau. Let me surface this to the advisor before deciding the operating point.

def time_eager(B):

def _tile_train_data(data, B):
    """DETERMINISTIC repeat-tile the TRAIN split (tx, ty) of a race data tuple up
    to exactly B rows (owner directive R2.4 item 2: "tile data if dataset<max;
    full-batch repeated/tiled deterministically"). The race train functions consume
    the WHOLE (tx, ty) every step (full-batch grokking), so a larger tx/ty IS a
    larger train batch — this is the only surface needed to drive the megakernel /
    eager paths at B without touching the train loop.

    Tiling is index-only (``idx = arange(B) % n_train``) — NO RNG, NO new samples:
    sample i appears ⌈B/n⌉ times, byte-identical across runs, so the wall, FLOPs/step
    and peak VRAM are reproducible. If B <= n_train we truncate (never upsample past
    the requested B). The eval/val/test splits (vax..tey) pass through UNCHANGED —
    the roofline disables eval (eval_every=1e9) so they are never touched; keeping
    them intact preserves the train-fn signature.

    data = (tx, ty, vax, vay, tex, tey). Returns the same tuple with tx, ty tiled.
    """
    import torch
    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
    n = tx.shape[0]
    if B is None or B == n:
        return data
    idx = torch.arange(B, device=tx.device) % n     # deterministic, RNG-free
    return (tx[idx], ty[idx]) + tuple(data[2:])

#!/bin/bash
# Re-SIGSTOP the tuner fleet tightly so the roofline measurement window stays quiet.

| B | TC megakernel (samples/s) | eager-lion (samples/s) | TC peak VRAM | eager peak VRAM |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 116 098 | — | 0.25 GB | — |
| 2048 | **142 477** (≈peak) | — | 0.52 GB | — |

**The throughput (= achieved FLOP/s, FLOPs linear in B) of the one-CTA-per-SM TC
megakernel SATURATES at B≈2k and DECLINES past 16k** — it is occupancy-pinned (one CTA
per SM; one 16-row dW atom × 132 SMs ≈ 2112 = one tile per SM), so a bigger batch only
adds grid-stride iterations with no occupancy gain, and cache pressure slowly costs it.
**Batch does NOT move the megakernel's roofline fraction** — the path to a higher fraction
is multi-CTA-per-tensor tiling (the structural fix), NOT a larger batch.

Eager (cuBLAS batched GEMMs) is *not* occupancy-capped, so it keeps climbing to a ~32–65k
plateau. **B = 16384 is the chosen shared operating point**: the owner's stated floor, ≈
one 128-row tile per 132 SMs, the megakernel within 3.5% of its peak, and eager at its
utilization knee (fair to both). Going past 16k *hurts* the megakernel and the metric is
megakernel distance-to-roofline — so 16384 is the ceiling too.

**VRAM is NOT the binding constraint at d=128.** Literal memory-max ≈ B~1–2M (tens of KB
